description: Rootless Packets-as-Code DSL & Rust compiler (v3.0.0) that compiles strict-lowercase .frasm code into deterministic, nanosecond-precision .pcap / .pcapng packet captures—and decompiles .pcap / .pcapng captures back into canonical .frasm code—across 81 native Layer 2 through Layer 7 protocols (2,611 verified .frasm corpus scenarios). Official website & interactive browser playground: https://frameassembly.ai.studio/. Companion to Wireshark/tshark, tcpreplay, Suricata, and Zeek.
rules: Every .frasm program must declare host <id> { [ip <ip>] [mac <mac>] }, parameterized flow <id>(<params>) { ... }, and compile { ... } (strictly one compile block; loop was removed in v2.0.0).

All built-in keywords, protocols, modifiers, and time units (ns, us, ms, s, m) are strictly lowercase alphanumeric without '_' or '-' (e.g., echorequest, innervlan, clienthello, hosthdr, transporthdr, sackperm, readholdingregisters); user-defined host, flow, and parameter names allow uppercase, '_', and '-'.
Always use inline wait <int><ns|us|ms|s|m> on frame statements; never use standalone wait lines, loop blocks, or +5ms / [+delay] prefixes.

Always use srcport, dstport, seq, acknum, ttl, qinq <outer> innervlan <inner>, and reqid; never use sport, dport, ack_num, or hop_limit, and never mix IPv4 and IPv6 endpoints in the same packet statement.

Use the v3.0.0 CLI: frameassembly <in.frasm> [out.pcap] (default root compilation; no compile subcommand), frameassembly show <in.frasm>, frameassembly reverse <in.pcap> [out.frasm], frameassembly help [subcommand], and frameassembly version (never -o or --output).
Always use // for .frasm comments (never # or ;); never include // PROMPT:, // TOKENS:, or // INSTRUCTION: in human-facing docs.
